entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
--------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Ashok Kumar Sinha (4), Advocate.

For the State : Mr. Naveen Kumar Ganjhu, A.P.P.
For the O.P. No. 2 : None.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned counsel for the State.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1148/2018 instituted under Sections 498-A, 323, 34 of the I.P.C., the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
Nobody appears on behalf of the opposite party no. 2 and as per direction of this Court vide order dated 06.03.2024, no counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of opposite party no. 2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that earlier FIR has been lodged against the petitioner vide Giridih (T) P.S. Case No. 223/2015 for the offence under Section 498A I.P.C. and other allied sections, in which final form has been submitted showing lack of evidence.
Thereafter, on protest-cum-complaint, again cognizance has been taken against the petitioner for the offence under Sections 498-A, 323 / 34 of the I.P.C.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.

The allegation against the petitioner is that petitioner is the husband of the complainant and after three months of marriage, the accused persons demanded Rs. 50,000/- cash and on non-fulfillment Rupesh Kumar Burnwal vs The State Of Jharkhand & Another ..... ...

1 of the same, the complainant was assaulted and her ornaments were snatched away by the accused persons and ousted from her matrimonial house.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record, I am inclined to extend privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1 st Class, Giridih in connection with Complaint Case No.
1148/2018 with the condition that he will furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sunil/
